challenges.name: notification-consumer-commits
challenges.title: Fix the notification consumer
challenges.description: Rice Rocket's notifications consumer pushes "Your order ... is on the way" when an order is picked up. With auto-commit, an OOM-killed pod lost 300 pushes; the first fix then re-sent pushes after every crash, and one version never caught up with the end of the topic. The editor holds `runConsumer` with its key blocks missing, each marked by a `// [ ]` line; the pieces include the buggy versions. Fill every line so that: nothing is committed before the batch's pushes went out; each partition's commit is the offset after its last handled record; and a push that runs again after a kill is not delivered twice (the push gateway drops a send whose `idempotencyKey` it has already accepted; the pod's memory does not survive a kill). Run feeds order events to `orders.v1`, kills the pod right after a push or during a commit, restarts it from the committed offsets and counts the pushes customers received.
hints: Write down, for one kill, three things: which pushes were already delivered, which offsets were committed, and what survives the restart. A lost push means a commit ran ahead of the work; a duplicate means the retry could not tell it was a retry.

Look at where `consumer.commit` can run relative to `push.send`, at the value stored per partition (the committed offset is the next record to read), and at what the dedupe relies on: a Set in the pod, or a key the gateway keeps.

An invoice consumer that charges cards does: fetch a batch; for each record `payments.charge({ amount, idempotencyKey: invoice.invoiceId })`, then `done.set(record.partition, record.offset + 1)`; after the loop `for (const [p, o] of done) consumer.commit(p, o)`. A crash before the commit re-runs the charges, and the payment provider drops them by key.

tests.name: No kill: every picked-up order gets one push and the commits reach the end
Killed right after the 5th push: no push lost, none delivered twice
Killed during the first commit: the batch runs again without double pushes
Three batches, two kills, cancelled orders: exactly one push per picked-up order
Killed after the last push: the restart catches up to the end of every partition
